title.from: A client API for apps: preferences, subscriptions, contact points
title.to: Library API for hosts: preferences, subscriptions, contact points

description.from:
**Milestone:** M3, public email and new stories

**Goal.** As an app's server, I read and change a person's choices through one signed API, and tell the service who the person is and their verified address.

**Build.**
- REST API with IAM auth, resource policy by `aws:PrincipalOrgID`; `config/clients.yaml` maps role-name patterns to a product. Prospectus's own registry hit the 8192-character resource-policy limit, so do not list roles in the policy. The caller's product comes from the verified caller, never the body.
- Identity: `PERSON#<id>` for account members; `SUBJECT#<product>#<ss1_...>` for signed-in readers of a public-reader site (a pairwise subject cannot be linked across sites, by design: Prospectus `docs/SECURITY.md`); `ADDR#<site>#<hmac>` for an email-only subscriber. Readers' choices are therefore per site. Staff and members share them across apps.
- Contact points: Prospectus has no email. On sign-in the app sends the verified email claim with the person's role, as the Papyrus newsletter test send already trusts its `email` claim. Admin alerts reach people who have signed in since launch; the console says so. The admin set refreshes at sign-in until kanbus-3e30d1 brings a machine route.
- Routes: `GET/PUT /v1/preferences`, `POST /v1/subscriptions`, `DELETE ...`, `POST /v1/contacts`, plus kanbus-c68e03's. No realtime subscriptions anywhere.

**Acceptance.**
Behave features; a caller from product A cannot read a person's data for product B.

**Depends on:** kanbus-222bcf

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Client API
  Scenario: A site's server changes a reader's choice
    Given a signed call from a site's server role about its own reader
    When it turns off new-story email
    Then that reader's choice changes

  Scenario: Another site cannot
    Given a signed call from another site's server role
    When it asks for that reader's choices
    Then it is refused

  Scenario: An admin joins by signing in
    Given an admin signs in to a site for the first time since launch
    When the site reports their verified address and role
    Then they are in the audience for that site's admin alerts
```
description.to:
**Reworked 2026-11-04:** Ryan reversed the architecture. No new AWS account and no central service; see docs/notifications-plan.md in AnthusAI/Caducus.

**Milestone:** M3, public email and new stories

**Goal.** As a host's server code, I read and change a person's choices through plain functions in the package, in my own table. There is no network API: Papyrus's CMS routes invoke the site's own function, and only the CMS role may.

**Build.**
- `api.py`: `get_preferences`, `set_preferences`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `record_contact`, `erase`, dispatched as function actions by each host.
- Identity: `PERSON#<id>` for account members; `SUBJECT#<ss1_...>` for signed-in readers of a public-reader site; `ADDR#<hmac>` for an email-only subscriber. All within one site's table, so the site part of the key goes.
- Contact points: Prospectus has no email. On sign-in the host records the verified email claim with the role, as the Papyrus newsletter test send already trusts its `email` claim. Admin alerts reach people who have signed in since launch; the console says so. No realtime subscriptions anywhere.
- A person who administers two sites has two sets of choices. Accepted.

**Acceptance.**
Behave features against fakes; moto for the store.

**Depends on:** kanbus-222bcf
**Related:** PPY-44721a

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Library API
  Scenario: A host changes a reader's choice
    When the host turns off new-story email for its reader
    Then that reader's choice changes

  Scenario: An admin joins by signing in
    Given an admin signs in to a site for the first time since launch
    When the host records their verified address and role
    Then they are in the audience for that site's admin alerts

  Scenario: Sites are separate
    Given a person subscribed on two sites
    When they turn notifications off on one
    Then they are still subscribed on the other
```
